stem: A group of similar cells performing a particular function is called a __________.
solution: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function.

stem: The two broad categories of plant tissues are meristematic and __________ tissues.
solution: Plant tissues are grouped into meristematic (dividing) and permanent tissues.

stem: The tissue responsible for growth in plants, made of actively dividing cells, is __________ tissue.
solution: Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells responsible for plant growth.

stem: The meristem at the tips of roots and shoots, causing increase in length, is the __________ meristem.
solution: Apical meristem is present at root and shoot tips and increases the length of the plant.

stem: The tissue that transports water and minerals in plants is __________.
solution: Xylem conducts water and minerals from roots to other parts of the plant.

stem: The tissue that transports food (prepared in leaves) in plants is __________.
solution: Phloem transports food (sugars) from the leaves to the rest of the plant.

stem: Xylem and phloem together are called __________ tissue.
solution: Xylem and phloem form the vascular (conducting) tissue of plants.

stem: The outermost protective layer of a plant is the __________.
solution: The epidermis is the outer protective tissue covering plant organs.

stem: The waxy layer on the epidermis of leaves that reduces water loss is the __________.
solution: The cuticle is a waxy coating on the epidermis that reduces water loss from the plant.

stem: The tissue that gives flexibility and support to young plant parts is __________.
solution: Collenchyma provides mechanical support and flexibility to growing plant parts.

stem: The tissue that provides hardness and stiffness to plants, as in nut shells and seed coats, is __________.
solution: Sclerenchyma has thick, hard walls and gives strength and rigidity to plant parts.

stem: The simple plant tissue that stores food and fills spaces, made of living thin-walled cells, is __________.
solution: Parenchyma is a simple tissue of living, thin-walled cells that stores food and fills spaces.

stem: Animal tissues are broadly of four types: epithelial, connective, muscular and __________.
solution: The four main animal tissues are epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissue.

stem: The tissue that covers the body surface and lines organs is __________ tissue.
solution: Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines internal organs and cavities.

stem: The tissue that connects, supports and binds different body parts is __________ tissue.
solution: Connective tissue joins, supports and binds other tissues and organs; e.g., bone, blood, cartilage.

stem: Which of the following is a connective tissue?
solution: Blood is a fluid connective tissue that transports substances around the body.

stem: The connective tissue that stores fat and insulates the body is __________ tissue.
solution: Adipose tissue stores fat and provides insulation and cushioning.

stem: The tough connective tissue found at the ends of bones and in the ear and nose is __________.
solution: Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue found in the nose, ear and at the ends of bones.

stem: The tissue that helps in movement by contraction and relaxation is __________ tissue.
solution: Muscular tissue contracts and relaxes to produce movement.

stem: The muscles that are under our conscious control, attached to bones, are __________ muscles.
solution: Voluntary (skeletal) muscles are under conscious control and move the bones.

stem: The muscles that work without our conscious control, as in the stomach and intestines, are __________ muscles.
solution: Involuntary (smooth) muscles work automatically, as in the digestive tract and blood vessels.

stem: The muscle found only in the heart, which works continuously and involuntarily, is __________ muscle.
solution: Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart and contracts rhythmically throughout life.

stem: The tissue that carries messages/signals throughout the body is __________ tissue.
solution: Nervous tissue carries electrical signals (impulses) to coordinate body activities.

stem: The basic unit (cell) of nervous tissue is the __________.
solution: The neuron (nerve cell) is the basic unit of nervous tissue.

stem: The tiny pores on the leaf surface through which gases are exchanged are the __________.
solution: Stomata are pores in the leaf epidermis for gas exchange and transpiration.

stem: Each stoma is bordered by two bean-shaped cells called __________.
solution: Guard cells surround each stoma and control its opening and closing.

stem: The protective tissue that replaces the epidermis in older woody stems is __________.
solution: Cork forms a protective outer layer on older woody stems, replacing the epidermis.

stem: Xylem transports water upward mainly because water is pulled up by __________.
solution: Transpiration pull (suction from water loss at leaves) draws water up the xylem.

stem: Blood is a connective tissue that consists of plasma and __________.
solution: Blood is made of liquid plasma containing red and white blood cells and platelets.

stem: The tissue that connects muscle to bone is a __________.
solution: Tendons are tough connective tissues that connect muscles to bones.

stem: The tissue that connects bone to bone is a __________.
solution: Ligaments connect one bone to another at a joint.

stem: Which of the following pairs a plant tissue with its function correctly?
solution: Xylem transports water; phloem transports food; the epidermis protects.

stem: Which of the following is a permanent tissue in plants?
solution: Xylem is a permanent tissue; the meristems are dividing (growth) tissues.

stem: The muscular tissue of the heart never tires because __________.
options: cardiac muscle contracts and relaxes rhythmically throughout life without fatigue
solution: Cardiac muscle is specialised to contract rhythmically and continuously without fatigue for life.

stem: Bone is a strong connective tissue that provides __________ to the body.
solution: Bone forms the strong skeletal framework that supports and shapes the body.

stem: Which of the following animal tissues lines the inner surface of the intestine and helps in absorption?
solution: Epithelial tissue lines the intestine and aids in absorption of digested food.

stem: The dividing tissue that increases the girth (thickness) of the stem is the __________ meristem.
solution: Lateral meristem increases the thickness (girth) of stems and roots.

stem: The intercalary meristem is usually located __________.
options: at the base of leaves or internodes
solution: Intercalary meristem is found at the base of leaves or internodes and adds to length.

stem: Tissues make multicellular organisms efficient because they allow __________.
options: division of labour among specialised cells
solution: Tissues allow division of labour, with different tissues specialised for different functions.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches an animal tissue with its function?
solution: Nervous tissue carries impulses; muscular tissue enables movement; blood transports; bone supports.

stem: The plant tissue that makes coconut husk fibrous and tough is __________.
solution: Sclerenchyma fibres make the coconut husk and similar parts tough and fibrous.

stem: Parenchyma cells containing chlorophyll that carry out photosynthesis are called __________.
solution: Chlorenchyma is photosynthetic parenchyma containing chlorophyll.

stem: Aquatic plants float because their parenchyma has large air spaces, a tissue called __________.
solution: Aerenchyma has large air cavities that provide buoyancy to aquatic plants.

stem: Which of the following is the smallest and simplest level of biological organisation among these?
solution: A tissue (group of cells) is simpler than an organ, organ system or organism.

stem: Muscle cells are also called muscle __________ because they are long and thread-like.
solution: Muscle cells are elongated and called muscle fibres.

stem: The main function of the phloem is to transport __________.
options: food from leaves to other parts
solution: Phloem transports the food (sugars) made in leaves to the rest of the plant.

stem: Which tissue would be most active in a growing root tip?
solution: The root tip has apical meristem, the actively dividing tissue responsible for growth.

stem: The tissue that stores fat below the skin in animals is __________.
solution: Adipose tissue stores fat and provides insulation.

stem: Which plant tissue is dead at maturity and provides mechanical strength?
solution: Sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity and give strength and rigidity to the plant.

stem: The tissue that lines blood vessels and body cavities is __________ tissue.
solution: Epithelial tissue lines organs, blood vessels and body cavities.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Tissues in Action' is that:
options: cells are organised into tissues that are specialised for different functions, enabling division of labour in multicellular plants and animals
plants and animals have the same tissues
solution: The chapter explains how cells group into specialised plant and animal tissues, allowing division of labour and efficient functioning of the organism.
